name: Prolifex
description: A growth factor cocktail that dramatically accelerates tissue regeneration by saturating wound sites with engineered fibroblast activators and angiogenic peptides. Prolifex reduces healing time for soft tissue injuries by 40–60% and is standard post-operative care for augmentation surgery, where clean tissue healing around implant sites is critical. A luxury formulation called Prolifex-A includes stem cell mobilization factors for bone and cartilage regeneration.
effects: promotes clean vascularization of wound margins
Prolifex-A variant adds bone and cartilage regeneration
decreases infection window by shortening open-wound phase
side_effects: localized heat and swelling at injection site during active regeneration
rare: keloid formation if used repeatedly at same site
very rare: off-target tissue proliferation in immunocompromised patients
fatigue as metabolic resources are redirected to healing
Prolifex-A may cause joint aching as bone remodeling occurs
duration: Active regenerative effect: 5–14 days depending on injury severity
cultural_context: Prolifex is what separates a dangerous city from a lethal one — access to accelerated healing is one of the most meaningful divides between tiers. Tier 1 inhabitants heal at biological baseline, meaning a bad augment surgery or a knife wound takes weeks. Tier 3 workers buy a Prolifex course and are back on the job in days. Black market versions exist but the growth factor chains degrade quickly without cold-chain storage, and a degraded Prolifex dose can cause more harm than no treatment.
story_hooks: A fixer who runs augment surgery out of a Shelf basement has gotten hold of a cold-chain shipment of genuine Prolifex — and every interested party in three districts wants to know where she got it and whether there's more.
A character is healing suspiciously fast from wounds that should have been fatal — someone is dosing them with Prolifex without their knowledge, keeping them alive for reasons that aren't clear.
The Prolifex-A supply has been cornered by a Spire medical cartel that is using access to bone regeneration as leverage over Tier 3 patients with degenerative conditions.
